title: HTTP
body:
*HyperText Transfer Protocol* — the request/response protocol the web runs on. A [[Client]] (normally a browser) sends a request made of a request line (method + path + version), headers, and an optional body; the server sends back a response made of a status line, headers, and an optional body.

HTTP is a [[Stateless Protocol]]: every request is self-contained and the server remembers nothing about previous ones. That's why [[Cookies]] exist — they're the mechanism for faking continuity on top of a protocol that has none.

It sits on top of TCP (see [[TCP Three-Way Handshake]]), and over TLS it becomes [[HTTPS]]. The pieces:
- [[HTTP Verb]] — what kind of operation this is
- [[HTTP Status Code]] — how it went
- [[URL]] — what resource it's about

The full lifecycle of a single request, from the JS that builds it to the response repainting the screen, is walked through in [[HTTP Requests]].
